children: Banco Santander S.A. Sponsored ADR (BME:SAN) will pay an interim dividend of €0.127 per share on Nov. 2, up 10% year over year, totaling about €1.85 billion; its €1.825 billion share buyback ended Oct. 28. The bank targets return on tangible equity above 20% by 2028.
Previous Week Recap
Dividend Rises 10%
: Banco Santander (SAN) will pay a €0.127-per-share interim dividend on Nov. 2, up 10% year over year, totaling about €1.85 billion. Its €1.825 billion share buyback ended Oct. 28.
CET1 Ratio Rebound Expected

: Bloomberg Intelligence said Santander’s CET1 capital weakness may be temporary, with organic generation expected to lift its ratio to about 13% in 2026–2028 after TSB and Webster acquisition impacts.
2028 RoTE Target Exceeds 20%
: Banco Santander targets return on tangible equity above 20% by 2028, supported by credit growth, operating efficiency and geographically diversified income.
Future Payouts Tied to Growth

: Santander CEO Héctor Grisi said shareholder payouts beyond its €10 billion buyback will depend on profitable growth and capital levels, with excess capital returned through dividends or repurchases.
Botín Urges EU Bank Reforms
: Santander CEO Ana Botín urged European policymakers to free bank capital and channel household savings into regional investment, proposing a competitiveness mandate for EU bank supervision.
Cembra Leasing Partnership
: Banco Santander ADR (SAN) and Cembra formed an exclusive, long-term partnership for pan-European leasing and financing programs in Switzerland.
AI Generates €194 Million
: Banco Santander reported generating €194 million in economic value from artificial intelligence through September, combining cost savings, additional revenue, and improved risk management.
Webster Deal Expands U.S. Reach
: Santander (SAN) acquired Webster Bank in August, expanding its U.S. reach to nearly 8 million customers. The deal leaves the ADR exposed to shifts in U.S. bank rules on capital and deregulation.
Target-Return Funds Attract €6.2 Billion
: Banco Santander (SAN) launched 11 target-return funds in 2026, drawing over €6.2 billion. The bank plans to keep offering them, with returns improving as interest rates changed.
